messages:
vijay: heads up — ran into a deadlock in the Go SDK generator when using a short-lived ctx plus automatic retry on auth refresh in our step-function sample. weird interaction between constructor cancel and retry backoff.
adrienne: ugh. shortest repro? sdk version?
vijay: vendored v0.14.2. repro below:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Millisecond)
g, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, modelID, opts...)
// client has an auth refresh retry which will attempt reconnects if handshake fails
// we then call g.Next() immediately
```
if the constructor ctx times out during handshake the constructor returns error but the auth-retry loop keeps trying and one of the retry attempts later unblocks a read path that expects a fully-initialized generator state, causing a goroutine to block on g.stateMu and effectively deadlock.
aj: interesting — sounds like two issues: 1) constructor cancels but some background retry task continues, 2) read loop can see partially-inited state and block.
adrienne: does auth retry live on the client or the generator? we intended retries to be scoped to new connections only.
vijay: in our case the auth refresh lives in the shared transport layer and is started lazily. constructor starts handshake -> handshake fails -> constructor returns -> transport's retry loop keeps running and later attempts a successful connection which races with generator fields that were never fully set because constructor returned early.
aj: fix ideas: ensure constructor either fully cancels all transport retries on context cancel, or ensure transport's retries check a lifecycle flag tied to the generator instance and only run when generator is in Started state. also guard any read path against nil/partial generator state.
adrienne: i patched locally to: 1) create a childCtx for transport that we cancel on constructor error, 2) atomically set a started bool after handshake success before starting reader. that prevented the deadlock.
vijay: added a unit test that simulates a successful reconnect after constructor-level cancel and asserts no goroutine blocks on state mutex. will include as part of PR.
aj: solid. Also update docs: call out that passing short timeouts to NewGenerator is an anti-pattern if your client has background retry logic. either use a background ctx for lifecycle or explicitly Start() the generator after you finish auth.
adrienne: agree. For API follow-up: consider making retry behavior opt-in per-generator or require explicit Start so retries don't outlive constructor. open RFC if we want bigger change.
vijay: will open PR titled "go: cancel transport retries on constructor ctx cancel + guard generator start" and tag @aj @adrienne. will include test + quick sample change in onboarding.
ciaran-bot: PR #8123 created  CI queued (unit+integration) — flaky runner may retry once :robot_face:
vijay: thanks — pushing PR in ~20m. :thumbsup:
